measures.what: body length and width (the rectangular case, not including the mounting tabs)
measures.reply: servo body length: 40.58 mm (the case, end to end, not counting the tabs); servo body width: 19.82 mm (the case, side to side)

measures.what: center-to-center spacing of the mounting tab holes, along the length and across the width, plus the hole diameter
measures.reply: servo body length: 40.58 mm (the case, end to end, not counting the tabs); servo body width: 19.82 mm (the case, side to side); servo tab holes: 4.58 mm (each mounting tab has two holes, open to the tab's end like a U); servo hole spacing: 44.61 mm (between the holes on the two tabs, from the inside edge of one to the inside edge of the other; I didn't measure the spacing between the two holes on one tab)

measures.what: height from the top face of the mounting tabs to the top of the output spline, and distance from the output shaft center to the nearest short end of the case
measures.reply: servo body height: 40.4 mm (the case, top to bottom); servo hole spacing: 44.61 mm (between the holes on the two tabs, from the inside edge of one to the inside edge of the other; I didn't measure the spacing between the two holes on one tab); servo spline: 5.84 mm (the output shaft, across its splines, where an arm would grip it; there's a smaller reading of 5.60 at the very top, and I'm not sure which feature that was)

measures.item: MG996R servo horn you plan to use
measures.what: which horn (round disc / cross / single arm), its outer diameter or arm length, thickness of the flat part, and the hub diameter and height
measures.reply: servo body length: 40.58 mm (the case, end to end, not counting the tabs); servo body height: 40.4 mm (the case, top to bottom); servo horns: four plastic horns came with it (a double arm, a six-arm star, a round disc and a cross), and I bought a 25-tooth aluminium single arm (the aluminium arm's hub is 14.66 across and 5.95 thick, the arm 3.86 thick, 34.62 from the hub's far edge to the tip, with 2.55 holes; I didn't measure where the holes are, or the plastic horns)

measures.what: outer diameter (calipers flat across, jaws fully seated, not at the tips) and width
measures.reply: I can't measure that. Use your best judgment.

measures.what: distance from the output shaft center to the nearest short end of the case, and height from the top face of the mounting tabs up to the top of the output spline
measures.reply: servo body height: 40.4 mm (the case, top to bottom); servo hole spacing: 44.61 mm (between the holes on the two tabs, from the inside edge of one to the inside edge of the other; I didn't measure the spacing between the two holes on one tab); servo spline: 5.84 mm (the output shaft, across its splines, where an arm would grip it; there's a smaller reading of 5.60 at the very top, and I'm not sure which feature that was)

measures.what: width of the arm near the hub and near the tip, and whether the arm's flat underside is flush with the bottom of the hub (or how far the hub sticks out below/above the arm)
measures.reply: I can't measure that. Use your best judgment.

measures.what: thickness of the mounting tabs, and center-to-center distance between the two holes on one tab
measures.reply: servo tab holes: 4.58 mm (each mounting tab has two holes, open to the tab's end like a U); servo hole spacing: 44.61 mm (between the holes on the two tabs, from the inside edge of one to the inside edge of the other; I didn't measure the spacing between the two holes on one tab)

limitations.wanted: Real positions for the servo shaft, the tab height, the hole spacing across one tab, and the aluminium horn's arm width. Also a re-measured OD and width for the bearing
limitations.blocked_by: The person couldn't measure these. I used guesses from the datasheet and typical values
limitations.why: The arm has to line up with the servo shaft and the bearing. I made the bearing upright slide in X and Y to make up for the guessed numbers, and added coupons to check the horn pocket and the bearing press fit
